parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
{{figure:fig_7_1.webp}}

The diagram shows the graph of the probability density function of a variable $X$. Given that the graph is symmetrical about the line $x = 1$ and that $\text{P}(0 < X < 2) = 0.6$, find $\text{P}(X > 0)$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A flower seller wishes to model the length of time that tulips last when placed in a jug of water. She proposes a model using the random variable $X$ (in hundreds of hours) with probability density function given by

$$\text{f}(x) = \begin{cases} k(2.25 - x^2) & 0 \leqslant x \leqslant 1.5, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases}$$

where $k$ is a constant.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Use this model to find the mean number of hours that a tulip lasts in a jug of water.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: The flower seller wishes to create a similar model for daffodils. She places a large number of daffodils in jugs of water and the longest time that any daffodil lasts is found to be 290 hours.
parts.text: Give a reason why $\text{f}(x)$ would not be a suitable model for daffodils.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
The flower seller considers a model for daffodils of the form

$$\text{g}(x) = \begin{cases} c(a^2 - x^2) & 0 \leqslant x \leqslant a, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases}$$

where $a$ and $c$ are constants. State a suitable value for $a$. (There is no need to evaluate $c$.)
